highlights.title: IMF chief urges governments to tighten belts as global debt levels soar
highlights.summary: Kristalina Georgieva says big economies will have to make ‘very touch choices’ as soaring bond yields hit budgets. Business live – latest updates. The head of the International Monetary Fund has called on governments across big economies to tighten their belts as soaring bond yields hit budgets.
body: Speaking in Singapore, the IMF’s managing director, Kristalina Georgieva, said global debt-to-GDP ratios were at their highest level since the second world war and on course to hit 100% in the coming years.
She said governments could not rely on rapid economic growth to lift the burden of debt – and instead would have to make “very tough political choices”.

Georgieva was speaking ahead of the IMF and World Bank annual meetings which are to be held in Bangkok next week. “My message to the world’s economic policymakers will be this: we cannot keep delaying necessary policy action – you have the tools, now have the wisdom to use them.

“And yet we don’t see decisive action in the high-debt advanced economies where the need of the hour is for credible medium-term fiscal consolidation plans, supported in some cases by upfront fiscal measures,” she said.
points: Kristalina Georgieva says big economies will have to make ‘very touch choices’ as soaring bond yields hit budgets.

highlights.title: Your Next Great Read Might Be Certified ‘Organic’
highlights.summary: Amid a sea of AI writing slop, a new stamp for “organic literature” will help readers to pick out books authored by real, corn-fed, free-range humans.
body: As scandals involving the use of artificial intelligence by professional authors pile up, a British startup has established a way for publishers to certify their books as “organic”—written by real people, no machines in sight.

On Wednesday, Books by People confirmed it had received approval from the UK’s Intellectual Property Office to begin distributing a mark that indicates a published book has been authored by a human. The stamp, which looks like a thumbprint, will be displayed on the cover.

“If people are going to be writing AI books or seeking it out for their own enjoyment, that’s their prerogative,” Esme Dennys, cofounder of Books by People, tells WIRED. “But if you want to read something that’s written by a person, you should be able to find that. We’re just trying to create that choice.”

highlights.title: Hamilton: Ferrari have to catch up with rivals on power
highlights.summary: Lewis Hamilton is urging Ferrari to improve the performance of their power unit for the 2027 Formula 1 season as the 41-year-old eyes a shot at a record eighth world championship next year.
body: A first Ferrari grand prix victory for Hamilton in Barcelona in June provided hope that he could launch a 2026 title challenge, but an underwhelming run after the summer break saw his deficit to Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli grow beyond 100 points.

Hamilton ended a streak of six races without a podium by finishing third at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday, with only a poor choice of starting tyre costing him the chance to use his impressive pace to battle Red Bull's Max Verstappen for victory.
Following that encouraging display, he explained why he has confidence in his team going into next year.

Hamilton told Sky Sports F1: "I think fundamentally we've got a great car, and that's down to an amazing group of people back at the factory, who are really intelligent and have made the right decisions.

highlights.title: "After an all-time low, we've started to return to growth" - Asha Sharma touts Xbox turnaround after drastic restructuring and many hundreds of layoffs
highlights.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has reportedly told the company that Xbox has "started to return to growth" following wide-ranging restructuring that has reorganised the gaming division and resulted in more than 1,800 job losses.
body: "We're making the right decisions to reinvest in the business," Sharma reportedly said during an Xbox 'town hall' meeting, according to a transcript seen by Windows Central. "After an all-time low, we've started to return to growth, more than two to three times what we were, and we expect that continue."
Sharma specifically named the games Gears of War: E-Day, Minecraft Dungeons 2 and World of Warcraft: Forever - all recent releases - as having had "strong" starts and contributing to this.

Sharma reportedly also said Xbox had seen a decline in hours played, player numbers and revenue at the start of the year. The situation has seemingly improved, with the decline in hours played apparently now stabilised.

On Game Pass, Sharma said Xbox's previous strategy had sent the service's profitability "into freefall". She's likely referring to Xbox's decision to include Call of Duty titles in Game Pass on day one, which later pushed the company to raise Game Pass prices in 2025, before cutting prices in 2026 at the cost of losing day-one Call of Duty.

highlights.title: Jaguar’s first EV looks just like its divisive concept car
highlights.summary: The Type 01, Jaguar's most important and divisive car in years, has arrived. The production follow-up to the polarising Type 00 concept, Jaguar says the electric, four-door grand tourer is its most powerful road car ever.
body: Even though the Type 00’s design chief was reportedly fired earlier this year, most of its aesthetic has carried over to the final car, for better or worse. You can’t buy it in that hot Miami pink though — didn’t anyone tell them GTA VI is almost here? It has the same low-slung silhouette, extended side-profile, and huge 23-inch wheels as the prototype, though shifting to a four-door design makes those proportions feel more natural.

On the inside, leather and brass detailing run throughout. A 24-inch OLED display sits behind the steering wheel, with additional 7-inch, smartphone-style screens in the central spine, one in the front and one in the back, with controls for climate, audio, and seats. With no true rear window, there’s another display instead, rising out of the “panoramic soundbar” to display the feed from a rear-facing camera.
points: The Type 01, Jaguar's most important and divisive car in years, has arrived.

body: Reed will tee it up at the Open de Espana from Thursday in his first appearance since withdrawing during the second round of the flagship BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth last month.
The 36-year-old - aiming to follow in the footsteps of compatriot Collin Morikawa, who won the Race to Dubai in 2021 - is around 300 points clear of McIlroy with five DP World Tour events remaining.
McIlroy is not playing in Spain this week but is set to appear at the DP World India Championship in New Delhi from October 15.

Reed has topped the standings since February after victories at the Hero Dubai Desert Classic and Qatar Masters sandwiched a play-off defeat at the Bahrain Championship, with the 2018 Masters champion also recording three further top-10 finishes.

highlights.title: OpenAI drops another batch of mathematical breakthroughs
highlights.summary: OpenAI has revealed solutions to a number of long-standing mathematics problems produced by an unreleased frontier model in a batch of 722 manuscripts, covering 372 result families that group related papers.
body: Solutions to ‘hundreds’ of open questions are said to be included in a batch of manuscripts released by OpenAI.

The results have been expected for weeks, although until now OpenAI had not provided details about which problems the model had solved or exactly when they would be published. In September, the company said its model had “resolved more than 100 long-standing open problems across most areas of mathematics.” The released papers and other details also include some summaries of the model’s reasoning, estimates of the compute used, and stats about the number of problems attempted. OpenAI claims the “average result” used the equivalent of three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking.

highlights.title: Sali Hughes on beauty: loose powders have had a glow up
highlights.summary: No longer messy and cumbersome, a new generation of powders blurs, sets and mattifies without the faff. I can’t remember the last time I wrote about loose powder because, honestly, there’s been little point.
body: A fine coating of loose powder locks down foundation and concealer like nothing else can – no bridal or TV makeup artist, dancer or performer would be without it. Now, seemingly all at once, a flurry of new generation powders are offering way more for your trouble.

Charlotte Tilbury’s new Airbrush Flawless Blur Loose Powder (£40) is so good that I think she’ll revive the entire category. Its finish is ultra smooth, refined and flattering, and the packaging dispenses with everything that’s annoying about loose powder – no shaking messily from plastic sieves into lids here. The weightless powder sits neatly under a fine gauge mesh and you simply roll over your puff (included) to pick up exactly the right amount, then press on to the skin – even under eyes, where it sets concealer without caking or creasing.
The word “blur” is thrown around like confetti these days, but here it’s exactly right – everything is softer and hazier. It also looks terrifically natural on camera.

highlights.title: Supercomputing researchers document evolution of AI hardware
highlights.summary: An ongoing survey tracks the latest AI accelerator systems to keep hardware relevant for Lincoln Laboratory staff and sponsors.
body: As artificial intelligence transforms industries and national security, understanding the latest hardware capabilities is important for maintainind technological advantage.

AI accelerators — specialized systems designed to speed up capabilities such as neural networks, deep learning, and machine learning — have been a major area of development for nearly a decade. Since 2018, team from the Lincoln Laboratory Supercomputing Center (LLSC) has been conducting the Lincoln AI Computing Survey (LAICS, pronounced "lace"). Six papers later, LAICS continues to summarize current commercial AI accelerators and compare their peak performance and peak power.

"About eight years ago, we saw a sharp rise in the number of research AI accelerators described in research papers and commercial accelerators being announced, and we started to get questions about them from government sponsors of the laboratory's work. That was motivation enough to start the survey," says Albert Reuther, a staff member at the LLSC, which operates and optimizes the high-performance computing systems used by thousands of laboratory research staff.

highlights.title: 25 Years Ago, One Iconic Sci-Fi Shooter Perfected Video Game Horror
highlights.summary: I recently blazed through the first half of Halo: Campaign Evolved in a couple of days, fully prepared to relive a traumatic part of my childhood. Despite some modest gameplay upgrades and a complete visual overhaul, it largely still feels like the same game as 2001’s Halo: Combat Evolved.
body: One minute, Master Chief is rescuing stranded Marines across the surface of a mysterious ringworld. The next, he’s sneaking aboard a Covenant cruiser with a sniper rifle, storming an island fortress to find a map room, or driving a tank through a snowy canyon. Dropships crash. Aliens scream. Cortana chirps instructions and quips directly into Chief’s ear. Martin O’Donnell and Michael Salvatori’s score transforms every firefight into an epic. Even now, I can’t help but thrash my head when “Rock Anthem for Saving the World” kicks into high gear as you storm the beach in the game’s fourth level.
Then the sixth level, “343 Guilty Spark,” shuts almost all of that noise off as the epic sci-fi shooter descends into full-on horror.

highlights.title: Disney+ to Name New Australia Commissioner, Keeps Southeast Asia ‘On the Menu’ as It Triples Local Output
highlights.summary: Disney+ is about to name a new commissioner in Australia and has not ruled out a return to production in Southeast Asia, Jon Wax, executive VP of international original television at Disney Entertainment, said Wednesday at the Busan International Film Festival.
body: Asked whether production would resume in markets such as Indonesia after earlier cutbacks, Wax said Disney+ is exploring specific titles there. “It is absolutely on the menu. We just need some time to execute,” he said.

Local versions of Korean unscripted hit “ Battle of Fates,” confirmed in development in March, are now in prep, Wax said. In the supernatural competition series, practitioners of shamanism, tarot, face reading and saju go up against each other. It became the biggest series premiere ever on Disney+ in Korea and has since led to a spinoff, “House of Fates.” Wax said the U.S. team moved quickly when Choi Yeon-woo, who runs the Disney+ content operation in Korea, and her team first brought the show to them.

Wax said the show felt culturally distinct, given the privileged position its subject holds in Korean society, “but every society on Earth has their practitioners of this. And we felt like if this works, this could be something that could be shot in other countries.”

highlights.title: Nicolas Ghesquière takes us into the future for Louis Vuitton show in Paris
highlights.summary: Models walk runway at the Louvre with flying cars hovering above as designer envisions city life in a warming world. In silk slip dresses, breezy vented tunics and gossamer layers of chiffon, the models on Louis Vuitton’s catwalk were perfectly dressed for an unseasonably warm October evening in…
body: This summer’s record temperatures were on designer Nicolas Ghesquiière’s mind. “The world is getting warmer, this definitely had a strong influence” he said.

The show was staged in an inner courtyard of the Louvre, the catwalk illuminated by the tail lights of a fleet of 34 flying cars in Vuitton’s signature Damier check raised on stilts above the catwalk.
The contrast between the futuristic set and the historic buildings was an elegant echo of the centrepiece of the Louvre, where IM Pei’s glass pyramid stands amid the French classical architecture.

The future is always on Ghesquière’s mind – his science fiction bent showed up in the models’ beaded silver fringes that were somewhere between space-age hair extensions and sun visors – and this season, he was thinking about life in the cities of the future, his models as pedestrians among flying cars. “I was thinking about a woman walking through traffic, and how in the urban environment we sometimes feel vulnerable and sometimes feel strong.”

body: ChatGPT’s teen-focused experience ‘doesn’t send alerts to parents when it should,’ according to an assessment.

highlights.summary: From their dorky parties to their weird walks, the movie holds OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and other stakeholders with contempt, while demonstrating their recklessness.
body: Artificial, the new comedy-drama about OpenAI and the artificial intelligence arms race, is a movie of weird walks.

As OpenAI cofounder Ilya Sutskever, Russian actor Yuri Borisov clomps around, like a geeky Frankensteinian monster. As the controversial OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Andrew Garfield bounces and skips boyishly—a gait that Altman himself recently commended for its accuracy. And as Elon Musk, Ike Barinholtz puts on a loping swagger, commanding rooms of computer nerds like some sort of alpha gorilla (a semblance matched by his long, pouting faces, which call to mind those old Bored Ape NFTs).

During the movie’s post-premiere Q&A earlier this week at the New York Film Festival, Barinholtz wryly described his character as “a person who walks normally.” Such are the awkward saunters of the march of history in the making.

highlights.title: Xbox Official Clears Up Grand Theft Auto 6 PC Rumors
highlights.summary: Recent reports claimed that Xbox would receive streaming rights to Grand Theft Auto 6, giving its platforms a major advantage for this huge release. However, Xbox Chief Strategy Officer Matthew Ball debunked the claim, confirming that GTA 6 will not be an Xbox streaming exclusive or available to…
body: Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the most hyped releases of the decade. To the misfortune of thousands of gamers, it will not be playable on PC on day one. GTA 6 is a timed console exclusive, only coming to Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation 5 on Nov. 19. PC players saw a light at the end of the tunnel when a report claimed that Xbox had secured streaming rights to Grand Theft Auto 6, and the game would be available on PC via Xbox Cloud Gaming.

XCloud allows fans to stream games from their Xbox digital library across various platforms. Unlike Xbox Remote Play streaming, players don't need access to a console for it to work. While it wouldn't be the same as running the software on their computers, it would at least let them play GTA 6 at launch.

It seems that PC gamers shouldn't get their hopes up, as Xbox CSO Matthew Ball has spoken up about the matter and clarified that Grand Theft Auto 6 will not be streaming on Xbox Cloud Gaming exclusively, nor will it be available on PC on launch. The initial story came from The Verge and was based on an undisclosed source at Xbox, reporting from a statement made by Asha Sharma during an Xbox employees all-hands.

highlights.title: ‘It’s hard to imagine the fires of July’: a bike ride through the Cairngorms in Scotland
highlights.summary: Wildfires raged through the national park this summer, but much of the landscape remains untouched – and autumn is the perfect time to go. In the Cairngorms national park, the bracken is changing from dark green to russet and umber.
body: The wildfire that began near Glenmore and Abernethy on 15 July burned more than 33 sq km (13 sq miles) of moorland and forest. More than 500 firefighters were involved; homes and businesses were evacuated; and the emergency response lasted over a month. Visiting now, it’s hard to see, or even imagine, the damage. Much of the burned area is high on the hill and far from the roads. It’s a huge loss but, in a national park stretching 4,528 sq km (1,748 sq miles), surprisingly easy to miss.

I have come with a gravel bike to retest new bikepacking routes with Kees Wouters and Yannick Ferbeek from Legendary Rides, which offers self-guided tours, and Bikepacking Scotland founder Markus Stitz, who helped develop the routes.

I arrive in Aviemore from Edinburgh on an electric Ember bus, which allows bikes to be booked on board, a welcome development in Scottish public transport. Soon I’m heading out of town through heather and Scots pines, my bike bags stuffed with everything I need for the next few days.

highlights.title: Xbox restates plans for next-gen Project Helix to be a "family of devices", stressing "many players will be on the go"
highlights.summary: Microsoft has reportedly reiterated its plan to have multiple Xboxes - of some description - for the next and 10th generation of consoles. The suggestion being that there's a main console accompanied by some kind of portable, on-the-go games machine.
body: The suggestion comes from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who was talking yesterday at a company 'town hall' meeting that Windows Central was reportedly sent a transcript of. "We are moving to a family of devices for Gen-10," Sharma is reported as saying. "There is not one device that fits all.

"We will certainly have a great console first," Sharma added, "but we also know that many players will be on the go. There are some things that we are the best in the world to manufacture, and there are other things that we will partner on. So, we will be sharing more about that as our plans develop. The operating system is starting to look really good. We're very excited about this."

This is not the first time Microsoft has talked about next-generation plans, nor about its desire for Project Helix - as the next-generation Xbox hardware is codenamed - to be a "family" of devices. Sharma said almost the same thing to the BBC recently, stating: "We've been hard at work on a great next generation and a great family of devices for Helix, and we'll share more soon."

highlights.title: A moment that changed me: I was heading for disaster on the Greek version of Strictly. Then instinct kicked in
highlights.summary: I was gripped by fear, aching all over – and still recovering from cancer treatment. But Dancing With the Stars was a joyous celebration of survival. It was an invitation I accepted in a moment of madness – and, over the next three months, regretted many times a day.
body: Dancing With the Stars, as it is called in Greece, follows the same format as its UK counterpart, with an identical studio, a matching shiny floor, even many of the same costumes that are hired out and circulated among the 70 or more international versions of the BBC show. Of course, it’s all in Greek – and in the season I took part in, Covid restrictions had been imposed, which intensified its strangeness.

I am British, but by the time of my appearance on Dancing With the Stars I had become a bestselling author in Greece. In 2010, my first novel, The Island, was adapted for a 26-part series, which achieved the country’s highest-ever ratings for a TV drama. In 2020, I was granted honorary citizenship by the Greek prime minister. All of this had made me a minor celebrity.

I never imagined the competition would be easy. The only woman older than me out of the dozen or so contestants was Bessy Argyraki, who had been a Eurovision entrant in 1977, while I was still at school. In the first week, when we found each other weeping in the ladies’, we became best friends. All the other women could do the splits, but we were still struggling to remember basic steps.

highlights.title: Portuguese authorities took 83 days to tell Rui Pinto his witness protection was ending
highlights.summary: Commission concluded in July threat level was low. Manchester City whistleblower given 10 days’ notice. Portuguese authorities kept Rui Pinto in the dark for almost three months about their decision to end his status as a protected witness and notified the Manchester City whistleblower 10 days…
body: According to documents seen by the Guardian, the special security programmes commission (CPES), which oversees Portugal’s witness protection programme, met on 8 and 9 July to discuss Pinto’s case. It concluded that the threat level against him was low and that the special protection measures were no longer warranted.

Yet it was not until 30 September that Pinto, who has been a protected witness since 2020 after agreeing to grant Portuguese authorities access to millions of files gathered before his arrest, was informed of the decision – 83 days after it had been made.

With 10 days’ notice, Pinto was left with little time to address a number of immediate issues. He needs to find somewhere safe to live and establish a way of supporting himself in a new location, while avoiding contact with family members.

The Guardian contacted the CPES on two occasions seeking details of the criteria and evidence used to determine that Pinto’s protection should be withdrawn. On Wednesday, the commission was also asked to explain the 83-day gap between its decision and the notification. None of the inquiries received a response.

highlights.title: OpenAI Is Pissing Off a Bunch of Mathematicians—Again
highlights.summary: “There’s a perception of mobster behavior” from leading AI companies, one mathematician tells WIRED as OpenAI prepares to release more than 100 new solutions to unsolved problems.
body: In August, OpenAI convened around 40 mathematicians to discuss what to do if AI outpaces human capabilities in the field. The company hinted that its powerful models had solved hundreds of long-standing math problems, say people who were in attendance, but company representatives assured attendees it would not release the solutions all at once—an assurance OpenAI spokesperson Lindsay McCallum says the company is “not aware of”—and, worried by how the community might react, sought advice on how to publish the findings.

Attendees responded with “a mixture of excitement and dread,” but the meeting was a promising first step, recalls Northwestern University mathematician Bryna Kra. The group, she tells WIRED, asked the firm not to just publish them in a blog or tweet, like they had done with 10 problems earlier that month. Instead, it would be important for OpenAI to publish papers explaining the work so that mathematicians could absorb, digest, and use the results, according to Kra. “Apparently, that input was ignored,” she says.

highlights.title: 29 Years Ago, 'Buffy's Worst Episode Ever Paved the Way for TV Greatness
highlights.summary: Part of why the streaming model of TV is flawed is that so many shows get canceled after just one short season. If that had always been the policy, we wouldn't have gotten most of the classics of television, as every show usually needs at least a few episodes to work out its early kinks.
body: In the case of Buffy the Vampire Slayer, its early-installment weirdness lasts for its first 18 episodes. While there are a few standouts, such as "Nightmares," "Angel," and "Prophecy Girl," early Buffy relied heavily on a monster-of-the-week format.

It's important to remember here that Buffy began its run as a mid-season replacement. All that was really being asked of it early on was to fill a hole in the network schedule. The show was initially made as a throwaway, and many of Buffy 's early episodes are deliberately disposable.

In addition to the vampires, Buffy and her crew spend half of the first and part of the second season working their way through a murderer's row of classic Western monsters. That includes witches ("Witch"), a gender-flipped Invisible Man ("Out of Mind, Out of Sight"), some species -flipped werewolves ("The Pack"), Frankenstein's monster ("Some Assembly Required"), and a killer mummy ("Inca Mummy Girl"). If Buffy was a 2026 Netflix original, it’s hard to imagine it lasting past its first eight-episode season, and “Inca Mummy Girl” is a good example of why.

body: Swedish actor Gustaf Skarsgård, best known for “Vikings,” has started production on his feature directorial debut, psychological horror film “The Cannibal.”

Skarsgård said, “There is no way to approach Bergman but from deep within the gigantic cinematic shadow the titan casts. Just like the main character David tries to break free from his demonic magnetism, so too the movie itself will attempt to break free in a playful way, by using his own artistic tools.”

Birro said, “When I was a young screenwriter, I got to meet Ingmar Bergman on his desolate island of Fårö. He told me about his demons and showed me where he kept them: locked away in the freezer. For 30 years, I’ve been longing to open that freezer door and let the demons out. Now the time has come.”
Producer Martin Persson said, “ ‘The Cannibal’ is a very exciting, fun and surprising film dealing with how much one would be prepared to sacrifice to make great art.”

highlights.title: Inside Sephora and Vogue Business’s Night Kicking Off a Global Cause
highlights.summary: At the Sephora and Vogue Business event during Paris Fashion Week, the beauty retailer launched its global initiative Project Hearts Not Hate.
body: Sephora kicked off Project Hearts Not Hate, its global initiative to tackle appearance-based hate with an evening in partnership with Vogue Business.

The Shangri-La Paris played host to an evening of conversations, cocktails and dinner celebrating the launch. “I wouldn’t call it a project. I think it’s more than a project — it’s really an initiative, a commitment,” Sephora president and global CEO, Guillaume Motte, said in his opening remarks. “It is actually the first time that as Sephora, we choose to champion a cause globally across our 37 markets.”
Left to right: Laure Guilbault, Deborah Yeh, Guillaume Motte, Emily May, Adelaïde Zulfikarpasic.

The executive continued: “People experience hate because of their appearance, and we want to fight back and help change those perceptions. With humility, we hope to achieve this together. While we don’t expect to change the world overnight, every individual can make an impact. As a beauty leader, we want to shape not only our industry, but also how we live and respect one another's differences.”

videos.title: Introducing the Decisions API
videos.summary: Introducing the Decisions API: a fast way to turn text and images into actions in your app. Give the model an input, define a question and the possible answers, and use its choice to decide what happens next.
body: Powered by GPT-6 Luna, the Decisions API focuses on a small set of choices to make interactions feel responsive. See how it works alongside GPT-Live-1 and a Microduck to bring voice, visual understanding, and quick decisions together.
